editorial:
Ever wondered what it would be like to talk to people who have already passed away? You get to see that world through Ayumi, a high school student with a very strange family business. His grandmother teaches him how to be a tsunagu, which is basically a human bridge between the living and the dead. The movie has a very calm and soft feeling to it, focusing on the emotions of people who are grieving and just want one last conversation. It is not a scary ghost movie, but rather a sweet and sad look at how we say goodbye to the people we love.

What really makes this work is the acting and the slow, steady pace that lets you feel every emotion. While it might feel a bit slow for some, the emotional payoff is totally worth it. If you like stories that make you cry and think about life, you will love this.
endingExplained: At the end, Ayumi helps several clients find peace by delivering final messages from their loved ones. He realizes that being a bridge is not just about the magic, but about helping the living move forward. The movie wraps up with Ayumi accepting his role and his relationship with his grandmother. He learns that while death is sad, the love people leave behind is what truly matters in the end.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves touching stories about family and grief.
